'''Jean-François Callet''' (25 October 1744 – 14 November 1798) was a French professor of mathematics who wrote an influential compilation of [[logarithm|logarithmic]] tables and taught [[spherical trigonometry]] and navigation. 

Callet was born in Versailles and became a professor of hydrographic engineering.<ref>{{cite book|title=Biographie universelle, ou Dictionnaire historique des hommes qui se sont fait un nom par leur génie, leurs talents, leurs erreurs ou leurs crimes. Édition revue et continuée jusqu'en 1848, sous la direction de M. Ch. Weiss. Tome II|author=Feller, Francois Xavier de|place=Paris| publisher=Leroux, Jouby |year=1850|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k65238242/f348|page=338|lang=fr}}</ref> His most influential work was ''Tables Portatives de Logarithmes'', published in 1795: a compilation of logarithmic tables, based on the work of [[William Gardiner (mathematician)|William Gardiner]], which remained in print until 1906. Its roughly 800 pages give logarithms of the sine, cosine and tangent, as well as natural sines and cosines.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Archibald |first=Raymond Clare |date=1943 |title=Tables of Trigonometric Functions in Non-Sexagesimal Arguments |url=https://www.ams.org/mcom/1943-01-002/S0025-5718-43-99136-7/ |journal=Mathematics of Computation |language=en |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=33–44 |doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-43-99136-7 |issn=0025-5718|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |title=A reconstruction of Edward Sang's table of logarithmic sines and tangents (K43,1888) |url=https://inria.hal.science/hal-03106597 |publisher=LORIA (Université de Lorraine, CNRS, INRIA) |date=2020 |degree=report |language=en |first=Denis |last=Roegel}}</ref> It was influential, leading to other improved tables such as those of [[Edward Sang]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Craik |first=Alex D.D. |date=2003 |title=The logarithmic tables of Edward Sang and his daughters |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0315086002000186 |journal=Historia Mathematica |language=en |volume=30 |issue=1 |pages=47–84 |doi=10.1016/S0315-0860(02)00018-6|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Another of Callet's works was a spherical trigonometry text for use in navigation, published in 1798 and written in collaboration with instrument maker Jean François Richer, who was attempting to create a navigation instrument called the trigonometric compass in his application for the Abbé Raynal Prize. The prize was then being offered for a reliable and accurate method to reduce the apparent distance between two stars to the true distance, which could be used to determine the longitude of a ship's position. Richer's application won the 1791 prize.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Thümmel, O.|year=2017|lang=de|title= Der trigonometrische Zirkel des Bürgers Richer: eine Episode aus der Geschichte der Navigation.| journal=Deutsches Schiffahrtsarchiv| volume=40|pages= 249-294|url= https://nbn-resolving.org/urn:nbn:de:0168-ssoar-83137-3}}</ref>
